title: The NRI's Guide to World Cup 2026 at NRG Stadium, Houston
excerpt: Match schedule featuring Germany and Portugal, Houston's legendary Mahatma Gandhi District on Hillcroft, Sugar Land's desi scene, METRORail tips, and everything Space City's Indian community needs for the World Cup.
body:
Houston's Mahatma Gandhi District is one of the most iconic South Asian neighborhoods in the country — and now the World Cup is coming to NRG Stadium, just 6 miles east. With 5 group stage matches featuring Germany, Portugal, and the Netherlands, plus some of the best Indian food in America on Hillcroft Avenue, Houston is an NRI World Cup dream.

Match Schedule

| Date | Match | Kickoff (CT) | |------|-------|-------------| | Sat, Jun 14 | Germany vs Curaçao | 12:00 PM | | Tue, Jun 17 | Portugal vs DR Congo | 12:00 PM | | Fri, Jun 20 | Netherlands vs Sweden | 12:00 PM | | Mon, Jun 23 | Portugal vs Uzbekistan | 12:00 PM | | Thu, Jun 26 | Cape Verde vs Saudi Arabia | 7:00 PM |

Where to Eat: The Mahatma Gandhi District

Hillcroft Avenue — Houston's Little India (6 miles from NRG): This is the real thing. The Mahatma Gandhi District runs along Hillcroft between Harwin Dr and the Southwest Freeway, officially named in 2010.

Himalaya Restaurant is a Houston legend — Chef Kaiser Lashkari's lamb vindaloo and biryani have been featured in the NYT and Houston Chronicle Top 100. Shri Balaji Bhavan is the best South Indian in town — masala dosa and Madras thali, also Houston Chronicle Top 100 for four straight years. Chowpatty Chat for authentic Bombay-style pani puri and bhel puri. Angara Kabab & Karahi has the only authentic Hyderabadi biryani in Houston and stays open until 2 AM on weekends.

Raja Sweets is the oldest Indian sweet shop in Texas, established in 1986 — gulab jamun, jalebi, and rasmalai featured on the Travel Channel and in the New York Times.

Sugar Land (20 miles SW): Massive Indian American population. Saravanaa Bhavan for reliable global-chain South Indian. Nirmanz Food Boutique for gorgeous Gujarati food with Bollywood-themed decor. Desi District for Andhra food open late with weekend brunch.

Stafford (15 miles SW): Home to the BAPS Mandir. Shayona Cafe inside the temple campus serves pure vegetarian chaat, samosa, and thali — all proceeds support the temple. Mallu Bros for Kerala fish masala. One More Bar & Grill has multiple TVs and stays open until 2 AM — perfect for watching other World Cup matches.

Upscale Houston: Kiran's on Richmond Ave for fine dining Indian (4.6 stars, private dining rooms). Verandah on Kirby Dr for what many call the best Indian food in Texas — dinner only, reservations essential.

Getting There

METRORail Red Line: The cheapest option. Take the Red Line to NRG Park/Fannin South Station, then walk or shuttle to the stadium. $1.25 one-way. Runs from downtown Houston in about 20 minutes.

Park & Ride Shuttles: Multiple locations across Houston with advance-purchase passes.

Driving & Parking: Pre-purchase required. NRG Park has multiple lots but expect $50-150+ on match days. The Kirby/610 area gets congested — allow extra time.

Rideshare: Designated zones near NRG. Budget $20-40 from downtown, but expect surge pricing post-match.

Where to Stay

Galleria/Upper Kirby (5-10 min): Upscale hotels with easy access to NRG and great dining. Kiran's and Verandah are in this corridor.

Medical Center/NRG Area (Walking distance): Closest hotels. Hilton Houston Post Oak, Marriott at NRG, Holiday Inn NRG.

Sugar Land (20 min): Best NRI home base — massive Indian community, temples, grocery stores, and restaurants. Extended Stay options popular with families.

Desi Community

BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Stafford is a stunning temple with Shayona Cafe on campus. Sri Meenakshi Temple in Pearland is one of the oldest Hindu temples in the US. Patel Brothers on Fondren Rd near Hillcroft has everything for Indian groceries.

The Mahatma Gandhi District isn't just restaurants — it's Indian grocery stores, sweet shops, clothing stores, jewelry shops, and community gathering spaces. Walking down Hillcroft feels like being in an Indian city.

Tickets

Available at FIFA.com/tickets. Germany vs Curaçao (Jun 14) and Portugal matches will be popular with the diverse Houston international community.
author: Diaspora Desk
